page: Amazon Web Services m8id.24xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs. Operating at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz, this x86_64 architecture server features 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes 5700 GB of local NVMe SSD instance store volumes and a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate top-tier performance in multi-threaded workloads and memory operations. The server achieves top-tier rankings in Passmark CPU score, database operations, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier performance for both small and large block read-only operations, alongside strong write performance. Single-core performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring in the average range, while multi-core stress-ng performance ranks in the top 25%.

The CPU supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. These extensions contribute to top-tier prompt processing speeds during LLM inference across small, medium, and large models. However, text generation speeds for small and large models drop to average levels, highlighting a tradeoff between initial prompt ingestion and sequential token generation. The instance also excels in static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations, both ranking in the top 10%.

Given the high density of DDR5 memory, dedicated compute cores, and a substantial 5.7 TB local NVMe SSD storage allocation, the m8id.24xlarge offers high resource density for data-intensive applications. It is highly suitable for high-throughput database operations, software compilation, large-scale web serving, and memory-bound general-purpose enterprise workloads.

With a 40 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this server provides a balanced resource profile.
